What is the earliest symptom of vitamin A deficiency?
Foamy grey-white patches on the temporal bulbar conjunctiva (stage X1B).
What is the most severe eye stage of vitamin A deficiency?
Keratomalacia: ulceration and melting of the cornea, leading to blindness.
What is the skin sign of vitamin A deficiency?
The vitamin A dose for age, by mouth, on day 1, day 2 and day 14.
What is the vitamin A treatment dose for a child aged 12 months or older?
200 000 IU (100 000 IU at 6–11 months; 50 000 IU under 6 months).
How is vitamin A given in measles?
Every child with measles receives the dose for age on day 1 and day 2.
What is the vitamin A supplementation schedule (WHO, EPI)?
100 000 IU at 6–11 months, then 200 000 IU every 6 months until 5 years of age.
What are the features of acute vitamin A toxicity?
Raised intracranial pressure: a bulging fontanelle and vomiting.
What are the features of chronic vitamin A toxicity?
Hair loss, dry itchy skin, bone pain and a large liver. Vitamin A is teratogenic in pregnancy.
What is the zinc dose in diarrhoea?
Under 6 months: 10 mg daily. From 6 months: 20 mg daily. It is given for 10–14 days.
What is the benefit of zinc in diarrhoea?
It shortens the episode and prevents new episodes for 2–3 months.

What is the triad of acrodermatitis enteropathica?
A rash around the mouth, anus, hands and feet; diarrhoea; and hair loss.

Deaf-mutism, intellectual disability, short stature and spasticity.
What are the effects of iodine deficiency in children?
Goitre, hypothyroidism and poor school performance.

What are the effects of too little and too much fluoride?
Too little causes dental caries; too much causes mottled teeth (fluorosis).
What does thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency cause?
Beriberi: wet beriberi (heart failure and oedema) or dry beriberi (neuropathy).
What does riboflavin (vitamin B2) deficiency cause?
Angular stomatitis, cheilosis, glossitis and vascularisation of the cornea.
What are the features of pellagra, and which vitamin is deficient?
Dermatitis of sun-exposed skin, diarrhoea and dementia; it is niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency.
What does pyridoxine (vitamin B6) deficiency cause?
Seizures in infants, peripheral neuropathy during isoniazid treatment and microcytic anaemia.
